narr: An upper level disturbance passing along a stationary front draped across the lower Mid-Atlantic region triggered spotty thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening of July 31st. Of particular note was the deep tropical moisture situated across the region, with precipitable water values across the Piedmont estimated to be around 2.2 inches per Storm Prediction Center Meso-Analysis, or about 2 standard deviations above normal for late July. Though few, there were breaks in the cloud cover during the afternoon and early evening, which allowed for increased surface heating, with surface-based CAPE values rising to 2,000 J/Kg prior to the storm. Windflow in the low levels of the atmosphere was nearly unidirectional from the west, which promoted a brief period of training with a second cell developing around 9:00 PM EDT just behind the initial cell to prolong the heavy rainfall across the southern end of Lynchburg.
ev: Multiple roads in the Timberlake community were flooded and briefly impassible due to heavy rain, some roads observed with several inches of water flowing across or down them. No damage was reported with this flooding.
lsr: MULTIPLE ROADS IN THE TIMBERLAKE AREA WERE FLOODED AND IMPASSIBLE DUE TO HEAVY RAIN, SOME ROADS WITH SEVERAL INCHES OF WATER FLOWING ACROSS/DOWN THEM.
